subject: Stitch proposal: stack + bridge hosting window for Nimbus co-sell demo
messages:
From: Rajat Mehra <rajat@NimbusSystems.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, vanessa@redwood.com
Cc: partner-ops@cloud-si.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood x Nimbus - demo slot compression request

Hi Jonas / Vanessa,

Quick note from the Nimbus side after our calendar review: the SI that will join (Atlas) has tight availability on the 31st — they can only do a 60-75 minute window. Our joint engineering and product presenters need more runway to show multi-region failover (we typically ask 90m). Is there any way Redwood can compress host transitions and keep the show clean without losing the recovery demo?

We don't want to push the customer; they're only free that afternoon (CEST). If you suggest a plan (shorter host handoffs, a pre-recorded failover segment, or an ops shadow host) we'll coordinate.

Rajat
Director of Partnerships
Nimbus Systems

--
Rajat Mehra
Nimbus Systems
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Rajat Mehra <rajat@NimbusSystems.com>, Sofia Marin <sofia@atlas-sis.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood x Nimbus - demo slot compression request

Thanks for the heads up, Rajat. We can make this work without degrading the failover narrative — proposal below.

High-level: stack + bridge cadence
- Stack hosts: run two overlapping hosts (primary demo host + shadow ops host) for a 15-minute overlap during transitions so we can shave total runtime.
- Bridge segment: pre-record the actual failover execution (30s–60s), then resume live to show validation and KPIs; live Q&A remains at the end.
- Ops runbook: ops shadow monitors KV cache warm, tokenization latency; if the live failover raises anything, we cut to pre-recorded segment and then reconverge.

Concrete ask for Nimbus/Atlas:
- Can Atlas confirm two speakers for the condensed live failover (one for 2–3 minute live step + one to manage the validation checks)?
- Rajat: please upload the Atlas speaker availability grid; I attached an availability template for quick fill.

I've attached a short runbook draft and an availability grid (xlsx) — Vanessa/Karthik, help me fill the tuning parameters (batch sizes, expected warmup times) for the runbook.

If we adopt this, total slot target becomes 75 minutes (live + pre-recorded bridging). That should match Atlas's window and preserve the demo narrative.

Jonas
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook-draft-v1.pdf, availability-grid.xlsx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajat Mehra <rajat@NimbusSystems.com>, Sofia Marin <sofia@atlas-sis.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood x Nimbus - demo slot compression request

Love the stack+bridge approach — pragmatic and keeps the customer experience intact. Quick ops notes from my side: 

- Timing: to hit 75m we need strict segment cutoffs. Proposed segmenting (mins): intro 10 / core feature 20 / failover live 5 / pre-record bridge 2 / validation 8 / Q&A 30.
- Roles: Karthik: you'll primary the warmup checklist (GPU cache + quantization sanity). Soojin: you'll own fallthrough telemetry + tracing link-out during validation.
- Recording: we should produce a tight 90s recorded failover showing step-by-step state transfer; engineering can narrate. That will allow live to focus on the why and metrics rather than mechanical steps.

Attached: nimbus-mop.docx (ops contacts + run order) — Rajat, confirm the Atlas presenter names and give us a final attendee list. Also confirm whether Atlas prefers the pre-recorded segment be shown before or after the brief live validation (we recommend show-recording-first, then quick live validation).

I'll get the runbook trimmed and send v1.1 tonight. If everyone OK, I can lock the run order and share the recording checklist with Nimbus ops.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachment: nimbus-mop.docx
From: Sofia Marin <sofia@atlas-sis.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajat Mehra <rajat@NimbusSystems.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, partner-ops@cloud-si.com
Date: Sun, 23 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood x Nimbus - demo slot compression request

Thanks — this plan looks good to Atlas. Quick confirmations:
- Atlas will provide two speakers: myself (high level) + Mateo V. (technical, will handle the short live step).
- We prefer the recording be shown first, immediately followed by ~3 minutes live validation. That gives the audience the visual and then the “why it worked” live check.
- Attached is a filled availability grid (we used Jonas's template) and a single-slide checklist for the recorded failover.

Ops request: please share a point of contact for the Redwood shadow host during the overlap window (we'll forward any infra alerts there). Also we need the final run order and recording link 48 hours before the slot.

We'll align on final attendee list after you send v1.1 runbook.

Sofia Marin
Senior Solution Architect | Atlas SIS
sofia@atlas-sis.com

--
Sofia Marin
Atlas SIS
